C-CURSOR-TASK-IDENTITY.Summary: Origin: superseded C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL. Same F90 repair as that bundle, minus the F83 close-criterion trap. Discharge F90 as out-of-phase hygiene for RM-GOVERNED-PATH P3.1 (lifecycle finish). Stop every guessed task identity on a run event: lint argv token run-commands must not write T-000, and recover / auto-open must not invent T-001. Inherit a plan-declared task that is already in scope; refuse before write when none is. An explicitly supplied options.task is a legal first source when it is a declared id. cursor.unknown-task stays a correct checker. Do not write P3 step detail and do not amend the phase board.
C-CURSOR-TASK-IDENTITY.Problem:
F90 (decisions.md): the check ran and was right; the writer is wrong. lint with argv token run-commands records each MustPassCommand through appendCommandRunEvent (src/lint/core.ts:501) and never passes a task. The writer falls back (src/grace-cursor.ts:2977):
options.task, else last loose event task, else the literal T-000.
After a fold, run/ is empty, so the next command-run is T-000. The same fallback fires before any cursor event exists. cursor.unknown-task (src/artifact/grammar.ts:1365) then fires when run.xml names a task the plan does not declare. The position type says known task id only, never a guessed id (A13.2, src/grace-cursor.ts:252). T-000 is a guessed id.
Reproduced at HEAD c3d4b61 from sanctioned commands only, in a temp project that was deleted afterwards. The claim under test is not that T-000 can appear, but that the documented close order lands on cursor.unknown-task.
Documented order (ngrace-execute steps 4, 7, 9): open T-001, terminal T-001, fold, then lint argv tokens assertions final and run-commands. After fold, run.xml still names T-001 and run/ is empty. The command-run file is 3-T-000-command-run.xml. Lint is still green because run.xml has not moved. gate archive refuses no-open-epoch (1 loose event). fold then refuses unterminated range. Terminal of the event's own task T-000 plus fold writes run.xml Task T-000. Lint is then one error, cursor.unknown-task: run.xml names task T-000, which is absent from plan.xml. gate archive permits (run/ empty). cursor regenerate dry-run prints Task T-000, sources epoch=ledger task=ledger state=ledger. The catalog remediation for cursor.unknown-task says regenerate from the ledger and plan; that command re-derives the illegal name.
F90 is right that the transcript overclaimed unreachable. After the poisoned fold, cursor advance with task T-001 and kind terminal (no argv token open-epoch), then fold, leaves run.xml on T-001 and lint at 0 errors; regenerate then follows the last ledger event and stays on T-001. Avoidance also works: after the work fold, a T-001 progress event (again no open-epoch) makes the subsequent command-run inherit T-001. The documented open-epoch form with default from=1 after a prior fold fails with a range hole; that is why the natural reread of "re-open a declared task" does not work. The way back exists and is undocumented. The written order walks into the trap.
T-000 is a well-formed task id (ANCHOR_PATTERNS.task is T- then three digits). A plan may declare it. Generators emit T-001. F90's phrase that the plan can never declare T-000 is false as grammar; it is true of the conventional plan this close produces. The checker fires because the plan does not declare the id, not because the id is reserved.
Writer set that can emit an event whose task the plan does not declare (siblings, not only the run-4 citation):
1. appendCommandRunEvent (src/grace-cursor.ts:2977) invents T-000 when run/ is empty. This is the F90 emitter. 2. recover with argv token fix (src/grace-cursor.ts:616) uses last loose task, else invents T-001. After a T-000 command-run it writes a T-000 opened (inherit, not a new guess). The T-001 fallback is the same A13.2 shape, and it is unreachable: recover throws when looseEventIds is empty (src/grace-cursor.ts:595-599); listLooseEvents always sets task from the filename (src/artifact/run-membership.ts:48,73); the pre.looseEventRange non-null assertion at src/grace-cursor.ts:620-621 is the same empty check. Deletion is hygiene. 3. maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation (src/grace-cursor.ts:730) is the same last-or-T-001 guess; fold after a T-000 command-run auto-opens T-000. The T-001 fallback is unreachable: the function returns when events.length === 0 (src/grace-cursor.ts:715); a LooseEvent always has a task. Deletion is hygiene. 4. advanceCursor, pauseCursor, resumeCursor, recordAttempt, and recordVerificationUnavailable accept an operator task that matches T- then three digits and do not check the plan. They can write T-000 if asked. That is operator authorship; the checker is the detection. 5. foldCursor and regenerateCursor write run.xml from the last event or last ledger task. They do not invent a new event id, but they are how T-000 becomes the cursor.unknown-task subject. regenerate of a ledger whose last event is T-000 re-derives T-000.
A repair that changes only line 2977 and leaves the T-001 fallbacks is this repository's repeated defect shape.
C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL's approved spec recombined suite green, validate-marketplace exit 0, and post-archive lint 0/0 into AC-SUITE-AND-LINT, bound to the verdict by F82 and therefore unmapped. An unmapped AC-* emits change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped at warning (src/artifact/grammar.ts:1883-1890). The criterion required 0 warnings, so its own presence falsified it; mapping it contradicted F82. That is F83. The draft plan at fbc985f disclosed a Satisfies deviation to silence the warning. Maintainer ruling 2026-08-15: supersede, do not amend in place; that workaround is abandoned, not ratified. C-DRIFT-HONESTY already split this shape.

Goals.Goal: Never invent a task id on a run event (A13.2). One resolver for appendCommandRunEvent. Sources, in this order, only when the id is in planTaskIds: (1) options.task when explicitly supplied; (2) last loose event task; (3) run.xml Task; (4) last folded ledger event. Refuse before write when none of those is a declared id. Delete the literal T-000 fallback. An explicit options.task is not a guess; it is a legal first source provided it is validated against the plan's declared task ids like every other source.

Delete the unreachable T-001 fallbacks at recover argv token fix and maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation as hygiene. Inherit the last loose event's task when it exists (including an undeclared one already on disk). Do not invent T-001. Evidence of the refuse-when-absent property is a red on an extracted resolver; no public-API red exists, and the plan must not plant a fake one.

Keep cursor.unknown-task as an error for a run.xml Task or EscalatedTask the plan does not declare, including a genuine T-999 and including T-000 when the plan does not declare T-000. Do not exempt a sentinel id.

Make the documented repair honest. Catalog remediation for cursor.unknown-task must not claim that regenerate alone repairs a ledger whose last event is undeclared. Name the sanctioned recovery: advance a declared task with kind terminal (no default open-epoch), then fold.

Document the load-bearing close order in ngrace-execute (canonical and packaged mirror): argv token run-commands after a fold writes loose events; archive requires no-open-epoch; terminal the declared task and fold before archive. Baseline run-commands also requires a declared task already in scope. README.md and examples/ stay unchanged; no user-visible command table or example tree moves.

Constraints.Constraint: Binding: F90; RM-GOVERNED-PATH P3.1 hygiene only. Origin is superseded C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL. P1 and P2 are complete. P3 is objectives-only and NOT STARTED. This bundle does not write P3 step detail and does not amend the phase board. It exists so lifecycle finish does not inherit a close that plants cursor.unknown-task.

Ceremony tier T1 (module change). This spec stays status="draft" until a human approves it. Do not run gate approve. Do not write status="approved". This spec-authoring pass does not write plan.xml (F4). That ban applies only to this authoring pass. After this spec is approved, a later plan-authoring pass writes plan.xml.

Chosen repair is F90 candidate (a), which is also brief (a) plus the safe half of brief (b): inherit a declared in-scope task; refuse when none is. In-scope means, in this order, only when the id is in planTaskIds: options.task when explicitly supplied; else last loose event task; else run.xml Task via cursorNamedTask; else lastTaskFromLedger. Do not pick a plan task by position, by first-task, or by only-task. That would be a guessed id (A13.2) and is not brief (b) as ratified here.

Refuse is invalid-arguments, before any run/ write. The message names the missing declared task and the existing verbs that create one (cursor advance on a declared T-NNN so a loose event exists, or leave run.xml naming a declared task). Do not mention an argv token that this bundle does not add.

Do not add a lint argv token task. Inherit from a declared run.xml Task covers the post-fold close path. First run-commands before any cursor currently invents T-000; after this repair it refuses. That is a protocol change, not a new flag (F18).

cursor.unknown-task, its grammar site, and its severity stay. Do not add T-000 to any exemption set. If a plan declares T-000, that id is a declared task and inherit of it is legal; this bundle does not blacklist the token.

Folded ledgers stay immutable (D9). Recovery of an already-poisoned cursor is in scope as existing verbs, not as a ledger rewrite: cursor advance on a declared task with kind terminal and without default open-epoch, then fold. regenerate of a ledger whose last event is undeclared still re-derives that id; do not teach regenerate to walk backward to the last declared task (that hides history). Update the catalog remediation so it does not claim regenerate alone repairs this state.

Close protocol is in scope. ngrace-execute steps 1, 7, and 9 as written today run argv token run-commands without requiring a declared task in scope and then archive without re-folding. After this repair, step 1 must have a declared task in scope before baseline run-commands; step 7's post-fold run-commands inherit the declared run.xml task when one exists; archive still requires no-open-epoch, so terminal that declared task and fold before gate archive. Do not terminal the event's task when that id is absent from the plan. Do not document default open-epoch after a prior fold: default from=1 leaves a range hole (already noted in src/grace-cursor.test.ts around the C-JOIN-EDIT recovery).

F61: no two adjacent hyphen characters inside any XML comment body. This artifact prefers argv tokens over dashed flags in every comment; element text may name a dashed form but this file avoids that so a later comment cannot regress it.

F56 / F67: FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET is 4, so a task may plan at most three distinct fail signatures. FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET is 2 under exact kind-plus-key equality, so a task may never plan the same signatureKey twice. signatureKey names the property, not the file stem. F80: one red evidences one property; split inherit from refuse. F45: AC-CHECKER-HOLDS is true at HEAD; do not manufacture a red for it.

F82 / F83, following C-DRIFT-HONESTY (archive/C-DRIFT-HONESTY/spec.xml:633-671). Split the old AC-SUITE-AND-LINT shape. The task-observable half is AC-SUITE-AND-CI (suite green and validate-marketplace exit 0); a later plan Satisfies-links it to a task whose Verification includes those commands. The post-archive lint 0/0 half is close-verdict evidence, not an AC-*. An unmapped AC-* raises change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped (src/artifact/grammar.ts:1883-1890) and a Satisfies-linked close-time lint AC is the defect F82 records. This spec does not author AC-SUITE-AND-LINT and must not Satisfies-link lint-after-archive to any task. The close verdict quotes the 0/0 counts. Neither half requires a state that its own presence falsifies.
F66: README.md and examples/ are decided below as NonGoals (unchanged; no user-visible surface). Silence would fail checkDocsAndExamplesDecision.
Do not edit docs/plans/**, the phase board, CHANGELOG.md, any version surface, or .ngrace/changes/archive/**. Packaged version at authoring: 6.2.0. No product version bump.

Stop and re-spec rather than touching src/artifact/grammar.ts cursor.unknown-task behaviour, src/gates/** archive predicates, regenerateCursor derivation order, default open-epoch from=1, or adding a lint argv token task.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Brief (c) / F90 candidate (b): declare T-000 legal and exempt it from cursor.unknown-task. That weakens a checker F90's own text says is correct. Take it only with an argument that survives F90; this spec has none.

F90 candidate (c): auto-terminate command-run events so they never become the cursor's current task. Terminal is a judgment (ngrace-execute cursor kinds). A special case for one kind is a fold-semantics change, not a writer repair.
Brief (b) as "pick a task from the plan" (first, last, or only ImplementationPlan child). Plans have no current task. That is a guessed id (A13.2).
A new lint argv token task, a new GraceCommandError code, or a new graph module.

Validating operator-supplied advance / attempt / verification-unavailable task ids against the plan at write time. Detection remains cursor.unknown-task when those land on run.xml. Prevention is a different product.
Rewriting a folded ledger, deleting T-000 events, or teaching regenerate to skip undeclared last events. D9 / A13.2: the ledger is the record; recovery is a new epoch on a declared task.
Fixing default open-epoch from=1 after a prior fold (the range-hole). Adjacent, already noted in existing tests, not F90. Protocol text warns; the allocator stays.
P3 step detail, lifecycle finish implementation, phase-board edits, D1 applied-status writer, or any other P3.1 objective beyond removing this inherited defect.
Planting a public-API red for the T-001 fallbacks. They are unreachable. A fake public plant is not evidence.
README.md unchanged; no user-visible surface. This bundle adds no command root and does not change the CLI Overview table. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface.
examples/ including examples/polyglot unchanged; no user-visible surface. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INHERIT-DECLARED: Task-observable; a later plan Satisfies-links this. After a declared-task epoch is folded so run.xml names that declared id and run/ is empty, lint with argv tokens assertions final, run-commands, and change set writes a kind=command-run event whose task attribute is that declared id, not T-000. Discriminating negative: today's 3-T-000-command-run.xml after a T-001 fold. HEAD today: writes T-000.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REFUSE-UNSCOPED: Task-observable; a later plan Satisfies-links this. lint with argv token run-commands and change set, when run/ is empty and neither run.xml Task nor the last ledger event is a plan-declared task, exits non-zero with invalid-arguments, writes no run/ file, and the message names that no declared task is in scope. Covers the first run-commands before any cursor, and a poisoned run.xml whose Task is undeclared. An explicit options.task that is absent from planTaskIds is the same refuse. HEAD today: writes T-000 and lint is green until that id reaches run.xml.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SIBLING-NO-GUESS: Task-observable; a later plan Satisfies-links this. recover argv token fix and maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation do not contain the literal T-001 fallback. When the last loose event has a task, they still inherit that task (including an undeclared one already on disk). The refuse-when-no-task property is reachable only on an extracted resolver: recover throws first when looseEventIds is empty (src/grace-cursor.ts:595-599); maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation returns when events.length === 0 (src/grace-cursor.ts:715); listLooseEvents always sets task (src/artifact/run-membership.ts:48,73). Evidence is a red on that extracted resolver called with no task. No public-API red exists; do not plant one. HEAD today: the fallback literal is T-001 at src/grace-cursor.ts:616 and :730.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHECKER-HOLDS: Task-observable stay-true; a later plan Satisfies-links this; F45, do not manufacture a red. cursor.unknown-task still fires when run.xml names a task absent from plan.xml, including T-999 and including T-000 when the plan does not declare T-000. Absent run.xml Task stays silent. HEAD today: already true. A change that exempts T-000, or that downgrades the code, fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REMEDIATE-HONEST: Task-observable; a later plan Satisfies-links this. ngrace lint with argv token explain and code cursor.unknown-task no longer tells the operator that regenerate from the ledger and plan is sufficient when the ledger last event is undeclared. Remediation names the sanctioned recovery (advance a declared task, kind terminal, no default open-epoch, then fold). HEAD today: remediation is regenerate from the ledger and plan.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PROTOCOL-DOCUMENTED: Task-observable; a later plan Satisfies-links this. Canonical and packaged ngrace-execute skill text both say: (1) argv token run-commands requires a declared task in scope; (2) after a fold, final run-commands writes loose events and archive requires no-open-epoch, so terminal the declared task and fold before gate archive; (3) do not terminal an undeclared event task to satisfy fold. validate:marketplace stays green. HEAD today: step 7 then step 9 with no re-fold.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-AND-CI: Task-observable; a later plan Satisfies-links this. bun test green for touched packages (cursor, catalog, lint, grace-lint, and skill-contracts, and any other test this deliverable forces). bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts exits 0. Existing command-run tests that open T-001 before appendCommandRunEvent stay green (they inherit the loose declared task). This criterion does not include lint. HEAD today: those commands are green; that green is the baseline, not this change's evidence.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/grace-cursor.test.ts src/lint/catalog.test.ts src/lint/core.test.ts src/grace-lint.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Red-first on AC-INHERIT-DECLARED, AC-REFUSE-UNSCOPED, AC-SIBLING-NO-GUESS, AC-REMEDIATE-HONEST, and AC-PROTOCOL-DOCUMENTED, each property its own red (F80), split across tasks so no task plans more than three distinct signatures or repeats a signatureKey (F56, F67). AC-SIBLING-NO-GUESS's red is the extracted resolver; there is no public-API red. AC-CHECKER-HOLDS is HEAD-true and is a stay-true regression, not a red. AC-SUITE-AND-CI is task-observable suite evidence. Post-archive lint 0/0 is close-verdict evidence (F82), quoted in the close verdict after apply and archive, not claimed by a task pass, and is not an AC-*. Temp-project close sequence from the Problem (fold, run-commands, archive no-open-epoch, declared-task inherit) is the integration shape; do not dogfood this repository's tree as that proof.

Assumptions.Assumption: planTaskIds and cursorNamedTask remain the public readers for declared tasks and run.xml Task. lastTaskFromLedger stays the last Event task in folded epochs.

writeEventFile always writes a task attribute. listLooseEvents always populates task from the filename (src/artifact/run-membership.ts:48,73), so a listed LooseEvent never has an empty task. The T-001 fallbacks are therefore unreachable at both public call sites.
An explicitly supplied options.task that matches a plan-declared id is authorship, not a guess, and is therefore a legal first resolver source. lint argv token run-commands still passes none.
